question: How many people will have applied to Kyrgyzstan's CEC to run in the January 2027 presidential election by the close of nominations (13 November 2026)?

calls.reasoning: Past Kyrgyz presidential races drew about 59-65 applications (2017: 59; 2021: 65, with 37 already in by 14 Nov 2020). In 2026 only 3 had filed by 28 Oct, five weeks into the window. It appears the B2 Kyrgyztest is passed before filing (Kasenov and Zhapykeev filed after passing; only about 5 hopefuls have tested), which removes the cheap random self-nominees. Japarov (exempt from the test), Masaliev (passed 24 Oct) and possibly Suvanaliev are likely to file, plus a last-minute surge and maybe a few party nominees. Median about 8, with a right tail in case the test does not gate filing. No prediction market was found on Polymarket, Manifold, Kalshi or bookmakers.
calls.dossier:
- CEC news page (fetched 2 Nov 2026): applications from Kasenov (14 Oct), Esenbekov (27 Oct) and Zhapykeev (28 Oct), all self-nominated; on 30 Oct the CEC registered authorized representatives for Esenbekov and Zhapykeev. No later filings found.
- AKIpress (5 Oct 2026): zero applications 10 days into the window.
- 24.kg (20 Oct 2026) and open.kg summary (28 Oct 2026): Kyrgyztest at B2 is mandatory. Suvanaliev and Zhapykeev failed on 8 Oct; Zhapykeev later passed; Masaliev passed on 24 Oct; Kasenov passed before filing. Retakes are unlimited. Japarov is exempt. About 5 hopefuls are publicly known to have tested.
- Japarov said (28 Oct interview, per question background) he will run and that 'quite a few' candidates will register by 13 Nov; he had not filed as of 28 Oct. Suvanaliev and Masaliev have signalled they will run.
- Last cycle: CEC notice of 14 Nov 2020 shows 37 applications already in that day (Japarov filed then); ODIHR gives the 2021 final as 65 applicants and 18 registered. 2017: 59 applications, 13 registered (ODIHR). Both counts are over all filers in a cycle where the language test was not clearly a pre-filing gate.
- Past cycles: the bulk of applications came in the final days.
- Resolves off the CEC's final count of applications received (withdrawn or refused ones count; documents declined at intake do not).
- Event window: about 25 Sep 2026 -> 24:00 on 12 Nov / 13 Nov 2026. As of 2 Nov, about 85% has elapsed.
- Status quo: 3 filers; continuing the current pace (~1 per week) would add 1-2.
- Searched without finding: filings after 28 Oct; party nominations; any prediction market (none found); confirmation that the test certificate is legally required at filing rather than at registration.
calls.reference_class: Kyrgyz presidential nomination periods 2011-2021 (CEC application counts), adjusted for the 2026 cycle in which a language test appears to gate filing

calls.reasoning: As of 28 Oct the CEC had 3 applicants (Kasenov, Esenbekov, Zhapykeev). Unlike 2017 (59) and 2021 (65), a Kyrgyztest certificate must accompany the application, so filings are heavily gated (18% first-attempt pass rate). Japarov is near-certain to file; Masaliev has passed the test but is noncommittal; Suvanaliev can retake. Kyrgyz races historically see late surges, but the test barrier caps fringe filers. Median ~7, right-skewed. No prediction market found (harness Polymarket/Manifold search empty; Kalshi/bookmakers not separately checked).

- Azattyq Asia / open.kg (Oct 2026): a Kyrgyztest certificate at upper-intermediate (B2) level must be submitted to the CEC with the application, i.e. the test gates filing itself. In 2017/2021 the test came after filing.
- 24.kg (Oct 2026): 2026 Kyrgyztest stats: 21,552 first-time takers, 3,859 passed on the first try (~18%); overall pass rate on all attempts 43.5%. Retakes are unlimited.
- Suvanaliev (ex-interior minister) and Zhapykeev failed the test on 8 Oct (Suvanaliev 56/60 on the written part). Zhapykeev passed a retake and filed 28 Oct. Suvanaliev had not filed per the sources found.
- Ishak Masaliev (Communist Party, ex-MP) passed the test (24.kg, late Oct) but was noncommittal about running; no filing found.
- Japarov announced on 13 Aug that he will seek a second term; gazeta.kg says he does not need to take the test; he had not filed as of 28 Oct. On 28 Oct he said 'quite a few candidates' would register by 13 Nov.
- Others mentioned as possible runners (Wikipedia): Madumarov, Sooronkulova, Umetalieva. Declined: Tashiev, Keldibekov, Babanov, Sariyev.
- History: 2017 = 59 applications (13 registered); 2021 = 65 applicants (18 registered), both without a language test at filing. Kloop 2011: 16 applicants by 21 July 2011 (partway through that window).
- Status quo: 3 applicants; the count rises only through new filings by 24:00 on 12 Nov.

But the 2026 cycle requires a Kyrgyztest B2 certificate before filing (Zhapykeev filed only after passing on a retake; Suvanaliev failed; first-attempt pass rate ~18%), and after ~5 of 7 weeks only 3 people had filed (Oct 14, 27, 28). Median ~9. Right tail allows for a weaker gate than it appears (in 2021 a certificate was also submitted at filing, yet 65 applied). No prediction market found.

calls.reasoning: Reference class is Kyrgyz presidential nomination windows (2017: 59 applications; 2021: 65). But 2026 appears to require a B2 Kyrgyztest certificate at filing, and only 3 self-nominees had filed by 28 Oct, about 5 weeks into a 7-week window. Expected additions: Japarov (near-certain), Masaliev (passed the test), possibly Suvanaliev after a retest, a few others plus party nominees, and the usual late surge, damped by the test. Median 8, right-skewed because in 2021 a certificate was also filed and 65 still applied. No prediction market found.
calls.reconciliation: All three runs agree on the facts: 3 filers as of 28 Oct, Japarov not yet filed, a B2 certificate submitted with the application, and 59/65 applications in past cycles. Their remaining differences are judgment calls: how many known hopefuls will file and how strong the late surge will be. The dossiers cannot settle whether the 2021 certificate requirement was as strict as today's (Run 3's point), so I widened the right tail for it. My distribution is close to Run 1's (median 8) with Run 3's thicker upper tail. I agree with Run 1's reference-class framing and carry it forward, adjusted for the gate.

disagreements.claim: Language test certificate gates filing itself
disagreements.verdict: Runs 2 and 3 cite sources saying the certificate goes in with the application, and Zhapykeev's timing fits that. Mostly settled, but 2021 had a similar certificate yet 65 filers, so how strong the gate is remains uncertain.

disagreements.claim: Size of last-minute surge under the gate
disagreements.verdict: Modest surge (2-6 extra) as the central case, with a tail allowing for a weak gate.
